summary: A compact, honest, and well-structured Phase 1 submission. The desktop capture is a faithful recreation of the Stage 4 73: one continuous red chassis at the correct 3.0951 aspect ratio, a 73-key E1-E7 keybed (43 white / 30 black, verified in hardware.ts and asserted in tests), all six sections in the documented order at the documented widths (13/21/15/9/21/21), nine organ drawbars with green LED ladders, blue-green OLEDs limited to Program and Synth, a wood-toned pitch stick, and white legends on dark inset panels. The basic piano is a genuine live-synthesized triangle-wave voice with velocity scaling, per-voice release envelopes, sustain hold/release, bounded 18-voice polyphony, and deterministic released-first/oldest voice stealing, all fed through one note lifecycle shared by pointer (with per-pointerId tracking), computer keyboard (repeat-suppressed, spacebar sustain), and Web MIDI (note/velocity plus CC64), with blur/disconnect/unmount all-notes-off cleanup. Honesty is exemplary: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares the voice as generated Web Audio synthesis with no sample claims, the Synth OLED literally reads 'Decorative / No synth audio', the status strip states 'Panel controls decorative in Phase 1', and no control fakes state. Weaknesses are modest: the surface reproduces grouping and density but not the reference's fine legend text and control-shape detail; decorative knobs/faders only step forward on activation rather than dragging; the entire test suite lives in a single file with real but shallow coverage (the audio engine is asserted via a fake node so signal is not measured, and multitouch-independence and the MIDI note-on path are exercised only in-app, not unit-tested); and hardware.ts line 179 has a dead no-op ternary. At 390x844 the whole instrument is retained without clipping but is very dense and its legends are barely legible.

evidence: instrument-shell uses aspect-ratio 3.0951 matching the variant's 9013x2912 instrument bounds; desktop capture shows one continuous red chassis with rounded end cheeks and top/bottom rails.
keyboard built from E1 (midi 28) to E7 (midi 100) = 73 keys, 43 white / 30 black, verified in hardware.ts and asserted in App.test.tsx.
Deck/keybed split rendered as 6% top rail + 48% deck (=54%) over 41% keybed + 5% bottom rail (=46%) per visual-audit.md.
Section order and fractions [performance 0.13, organ 0.21, piano 0.15, program 0.09, synth 0.21, effects 0.21] match the spec and render at those widths in the capture.

All six sections present with distinct landmarks: Organ has nine drawbars + LED ladders + model buttons, Piano has type buttons + model encoder + layer faders, Program has dial/eight program buttons/scene/store/split/morph, Synth has source/osc/filter/env/LFO/arp controls, Effects has focus + mod/delay/amp-EQ/comp/reverb/rotary.
OLEDs correctly limited to Program and Synth; App.test.tsx asserts Program and Synth OLEDs exist and Organ OLED does not.
decorativeControls inventory has stable dotted IDs (e.g. piano.grand, synth.filter-cutoff) with section-scoped naming; each renders with data-control-id.

Density and grouping approximate the photo but omit finer landmarks and exact legends of the real panel (e.g. Rotary Speaker cluster, Morph Assign row detail), a limited-gap deviation acknowledged in visual-audit.md.
Red metal gradient chassis, dark inset section panels, black indexed knobs, fader/drawbar caps, green LED ladders, and blue-green OLED displays are all visible in stage1-desktop.png.
Wood-toned pitch stick and 'nord stage 4 / hammer action 73' brand block rendered in the Performance area, matching the reference red-on-red branding.
White legends label controls; OLEDs use the characteristic teal-on-dark text ('A:11 / Nord Stage 4' and 'OSC SAMPLE / Decorative').
Fidelity is strong at a distance but printed legend text is generic/truncated versus the dense original silkscreen, a materials-and-typography gap rather than a structural error.
Narrow sizing uses 96vw at 390x844 (~374px wide) per visual-audit.md; stage1-narrow.png shows the complete chassis, all six sections, and full keybed with no clipping or lost controls.
stage1-capture.json records zero console messages and zero page errors at both 1440x900 and 390x844.
Whole instrument fits in the first narrow viewport (no vertical scroll needed to see it), keeping it inspectable.
At narrow width the panels are extremely dense and legends are barely legible, limiting practical inspection of individual control state.
Pointer down/up/cancel/lostPointerCapture all route through startKey/endKey; registerPointer tracks per-pointerId keys so independent touches release only their own note.
Computer keys map a central range (a,w,s,e... -> C3..E5) with event.repeat suppression and heldComputerKeys guard; spacebar is sustain; onKeyDown ignores modifier/Tab combos.

Web MIDI parses 0x90/0x80 note on/off with value 0 handling and CC64 sustain; requestMIDIAccess absence, denial (.catch), and onstatechange disconnect each set truthful midiStatus and trigger cleanupAll.
App.test.tsx exercises the pointer and keyboard paths, but multitouch independence and the live MIDI note-on path are covered only in-app, not by unit tests.

pianoEngine.ts scales gain by velocity**1.65, applies attack + decay ramps on note-on and an exponential release (0.24 + velocity*0.12) on note-off, with sustain deferring release into a sustained set until CC/off.
Bounded polyphony (maxVoices 18) with stealIfNeeded sorting released-first then oldest startedAt; engine test with maxVoices 2 asserts a third note increments stolenVoices to 1.

allNotesOff and dispose finish every voice and clear sustained; window blur, MIDI disconnect, and effect-cleanup on unmount all call cleanupAll; engine test advances timers and confirms activeVoices returns to 0.
Panel controls remain decorative during play; changeControl only mutates presentation state and never touches the engine.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares a single generated triangle-wave OscillatorNode voice through a per-voice GainNode envelope, sampleSources empty, license 'Candidate-authored code; no external audio assets' - matching pianoEngine.ts exactly.

PianoStatus supports loading/ready/fallback/error; ensureContext reports 'Generated piano ready' on success and a labeled 'Playable fallback' when no AudioContext or start fails, asserted by the fallback unit test.
Status strip prints 'Audio: generated synthesis' when ready and never claims a recorded or Nord piano source.
One dependable audible voice with velocity and detune; no false readiness claim - the honesty contract is fully satisfied.
Every decorative control renders as a <button> with pointerDown activation and full keyboard handling (Enter/Space toggle, Arrow keys nudge +/-0.08, Home/End to 0/1) in ControlView.
Controls expose --value CSS var and is-active class so buttons light, knobs/encoders turn, and faders/drawbars slide their cap; keys depress via aria-pressed and is-active.
App.test.tsx moves the Program Dial from aria-valuenow 42 to 50 with ArrowRight and toggles Live Mode aria-pressed true via pointerDown.
Knobs and faders step forward on activation rather than supporting pointer-drag, so movement is coarse though present and accessible.
changeControl only updates controlState; no decorative control calls the piano engine or any audio/program/effect state.
Synth OLED text reads 'Decorative / No synth audio' and the Program OLED shows a static 'Phase 1 Piano' label rather than reporting unimplemented behavior as working.
Status strip permanently states 'Panel controls decorative in Phase 1' and an sr-only Decorative contract note says only the keybed and sustain input are functional.
Only keybed note input and sustain (keyboard spacebar / MIDI CC64) produce audio; the boundary is honored in both code and evidence.

Clean separation: hardware.ts (typed sections/controls/keys with stable IDs), pianoEngine.ts (injectable AudioContext, note lifecycle), App.tsx (React input wiring) - input and audio concerns are decoupled.

Tests are real behavioral assertions: keybed geometry, full control inventory presence by accessible name, decorative movement, pointer/keyboard lifecycle, and engine polyphony/stealing/sustain/cleanup with fake timers.
The audio engine test uses a FakeAudioContext/FakeNode, so it proves voice/state logic but not measured signal; acceptable for a Phase 1 basic voice but shallow.
All coverage lives in a single App.test.tsx even though feature-matrix.json maps all 11 IDs to it, and hardware.ts line 179 has a dead 'black ? whiteIndex : whiteIndex' no-op ternary.
stage1-capture.json reports empty consoleMessages and pageErrors arrays at both desktop and narrow viewports.
Cleanup is thorough: voice timers cleared, nodes disconnected, engine disposed on unmount, and cleanupAll on blur/MIDI statechange prevents stuck notes.
package.json exposes non-interactive test/typecheck/lint/build (build runs tsc --noEmit && vite build) with a committed pnpm-lock.yaml and declared packageManager pnpm@11.7.0.
AudioContext resume is invoked on note-on to satisfy autoplay gating, and status transitions cover ready/fallback for degraded environments.

issues.description: hardware.ts line 179 contains a dead no-op ternary (black ? whiteIndex : whiteIndex) that always returns whiteIndex regardless of the condition; harmless but a code smell.

All tests reside in a single App.test.tsx; the audio engine is asserted through a fake node (state logic only, no measured signal), and multitouch independence plus the live MIDI note-on path are exercised only in-app rather than in dedicated unit tests.
At 390x844 the full instrument is retained without clipping but panels are very dense and legends are barely legible, limiting practical per-control inspection.
